title: Jellyfish UFO In Rainbow Over Alaskan Military Base Busted By UFOlogists; It's Not What You Think It Is
excerpt: Sarah Jane Osborn clicked and videographed what seems like definite evidence of jellyfish UFOs, but could it be something more ordinary than perceived? There’s no general consensus, but the viral Alaskan clip is probably not a mystery anymore.
content:
The jellyfish-like object that drifted across a rainbow over Anchorage in Alaska had social media buzzing about UFOs for over a week now. Seems like some of the UFOlogists have cracked the case, and it might disappoint the believers.

Sara Jane Osborn filmed the tentacled object in Anchorage on June 15, 2026, and the clip went viral recently on TikTok. Most social media users assumed it was a jellyfish UAP hovering above Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER), the US military base that hosts F-22 Raptors. In an interview, Osborn told the Daily Mail it was “very clearly not a kite in its movements.”

Is it for real or just a random kite? Sarah Jane Osbern, who was filming a rainbow over Anchorage, allegedly caught the tentacled UAP hovering over Joint Base Elmendorf-Richardson (JBER) in Alaska.#UFOs #JellyfishUFOhttps://t.co/hIEBKZd34i

— Mashable India (@MashableIndia) November 11, 2026

However, UFOlogist Jeremy Corbell’s Weaponized Podcast pulled her original reel, tracking the object frame by frame, and published its verdict on November 11. The conclusion was a tethered octopus-style show kite, at about 80 percent.

CGI or AI?

The frame jitters rule out CGI or AI at 95 percent, per the aforementioned UFOlogist's diagnostics. Some experts were also skeptical about the video being a CGI render. However, it has not been proved or disproved.

JBER not in the frame?

UFO analysts also argued that the camera's view was at the Alaska Geologic Materials Center sign on Penland Parkway in east Anchorage. That's not exactly JBER. Is it? The rainbow puts Osborn's view at roughly 90 degrees true, across Russian Jack Springs Park, with the object 1.2 to 2 km away, per the analysis. So, most definitely not over the Alaskan military base.

Kites, Always Kites

Jacob Israel posted a video of an octopus-style kite on X/Twitter and wrote that it is always kites. Meanwhile, Corbell posted separately that the jellyfish UAP he and George Knapp exposed is real military-filmed footage; however, it should be kept apart from these spurious clips. Several social media users also shared the alleged tentacled kite that could have been misinterpreted as the jellyfish UFO.
